subject: Oceanography
title: What Is El Niño?
description: A short lesson to help you apply What Is El Niño?.

hook.text: Every few years, the tropical Pacific flips its pattern—warm water sloshes east, and weather goes haywire.

buildup.text: Normally, trade winds push warm water westward—piling it up near Australia and Indonesia.

discovery.text: During El Niño, trade winds weaken—warm water flows back east, warming the central and eastern Pacific.

twist.text: Peruvian fishermen named it 'El Niño' (the boy child) because it appeared around Christmas, killing their fish catch.

climax.text: El Niño affects weather globally—drought in Australia, floods in Peru, and warm winters in Canada.

punchline.text: A warm patch in the Pacific rewrites weather across the planet.

quiz.question: What happens during El Niño?
options: Trade winds weaken and warm water shifts eastward
